The same applies to $2.03 a day / $9.94 a week at line 44 (the cookery note in index.ts:403), and to $18,200, 15% and $45,000 at line 68 (the tax constants).

claims: usually $1,119.10 a week (for 2026-27) ... less than $26.44 an hour. Many employers pay more, and enterprise agreements often do.
whys: $1,119.10 is typed into the prose instead of using STANDARD_WEEKLY_RATE, and $26.44 is typed instead of coming from the minimum-wage constant, so both will drift on the next wage review. 'Many employers pay more, and enterprise agreements often do' is a claim about how many employers do this, with no figure or source.

whys: The site cites the same decision number for two different years: '[2026] FWCFB 3500' 19 times and '[2025] FWCFB 3500' 3 times across lib/modules/app. One of the two years is wrong.
constants: Annual wage review citation constant (whichever file holds the AWR decision reference)

claims: First-year FAQ answer says 'the $67.15 industry allowance' as a typed literal.
whys: The value matches today, but it is hard-coded in prose while the page body and calculator read INDUSTRY_ALLOWANCE.general. It will go stale at the next 1 July update if only the constant changes.
reviewerNotes: Confirmed: '$67.15 industry allowance' is typed into the first-year FAQ answer as a literal. It matches INDUSTRY_ALLOWANCE.general in lib/data/apprentice-pay/spokes.ts:166 today, but the text will go stale if only the constant changes. Source edit needed, so this goes to factQuestions.

claims: On the threshold minimum, {APS_SUPER_RATE}% is {formatSalary(threshold.min * 0.154)} a year
whys: The super dollars use a hard-coded 0.154 while the label uses APS_SUPER_RATE (APS.superannuation.rate ?? 15.4). If the rate in aps.ts changes, the dollar figure and the stated percentage will disagree.
reviewerNotes: I agree with the writer's question. The super dollar figures use a hard-coded 0.154, but the label uses APS_SUPER_RATE. The calculation should be APS_SUPER_RATE / 100 so the two cannot disagree. This needs a code change.

claims: The National Minimum Wage rose 4.75% on 1 July 2026 to {aud(nmw.weekly, 2)} a week.
whys: 4.75% is the modern award increase. The site's own data says the NMW rose about 6.0%: NMW_HISTORY_RAW has 2026-27 published "6.0%", and EMPLOYMENT.minimumWageWeekly 1004.90 / minimumWageWeeklyPrevious 948.00 = +6.0%. The brief also gives the NMW rise as 5.97%. The percentage is typed into the prose, not read from code.
constants: lib/constants/minimum-wage.ts NMW_HISTORY_RAW (2026-27 published) or the computed NMW increase (EMPLOYMENT.minimumWageWeekly / minimumWageWeeklyPrevious - 1); the award figure is NMW_DECISION.awardIncrease
reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's fact question. The prose says 'The National Minimum Wage rose 4.75% on 1 July 2026', but 4.75% is the modern award increase. The site's NMW_HISTORY_RAW (lib/constants/minimum-wage.ts:129) has 2026-27 published as '6.0%', and the brief gives the NMW rise as 5.97%. The percentage is typed into the source, so this pass did not change it. It needs a human or code fix (read it from the NMW_HISTORY published value or the computed increase).

claims: From 1 December 2026 retail, fast food and pharmacy rates for 18 to 20 year olds with more than 6 months' service begin rising towards the adult rate.
whys: The start date and the 6-month service condition are typed into the text, not taken from a constant. Neither is cited on the page. Check both against the FWC junior rates decision for the Retail, Fast Food and Pharmacy awards.
constants: lib/constants/hospitality-award.ts (or a junior-rates constant beside RETAIL_RATES)

claims: The 12% superannuation guarantee is paid by the employer on top of award wages. From 1 July 2026 it must be paid with each pay rather than quarterly.
whys: The 12% is typed into the text instead of using SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate. 'Paid with each pay' simplifies the Payday Super rule, under which contributions must reach the fund within a set number of days after payday. Confirm this wording is precise enough.
